question: Can the 1/1 token image be the lossless WebP (data:image/webp;base64) instead of the PNG?

judge.reason:
Use the lossless WebP.

The deciding evidence was observed on mainnet, not inferred. OpenSea already shows on-chain data:image/webp;base64 lossless images on live Ethereum tokens:
- Tozzi Duck Machine 0x0cd9c257... tokens 200 and 201 (400x400).
- ShitPlunger 0x01cecf7a... token 1, an ERC-1155 at 1536x1536. This is the same width and encoding as our 1536x2048 still.

The precedent sweep and its adversarial re-check both confirmed this. For every token, the file name on i2c.seadn.io is the MD5 of the decoded on-chain WebP bytes, and the served thumbnail matches the on-chain pixels within about 0.7 to 3 out of 255 per channel. Other observations:
- Rarible serves the original WebP bytes byte for byte.
- MetaMask's NFT API hands wallets OpenSea's copy.
- DeBank, which feeds Rabby, re-hosts these tokens as PNG.
- The repo's own still.webp was checked to be a plain lossless file (VP8L, no alpha, no extra metadata chunks). Chrome 154 and system WebKit decode it to exactly the PNG's pixels, as does Apple's image decoder.

OpenSea's CDN also sends JPEG to clients that do not accept WebP. So even the old browsers without WebP (about 0.4% of usage, mostly iOS below 14, IE11 and Safari on macOS before Big Sur) still get a thumbnail on OpenSea.

Against WebP, in order of weight:
1. Gallery.so. Its published reference backend has no case for a WebP data URI, so the still would probably not show. The token would still display through the HTML animation_url, and whether this matches production or the site still indexes was not verified.
2. Alchemy is mixed. One of three WebP precedents decoded; two fell back to the collection image, even after a refresh request. The data URI itself is kept in originalUrl.
3. No precedent is anywhere near our size. The largest WebP seen was 10.5 KB, against 110,572 bytes inside a tokenURI of about 1.2 MB.

Risk 3 does not depend on the format. The 1.1 to 1.3 MB tokenURI, the ';utf8,' prefix and the '+' handling apply to PNG too, and PNG makes them slightly worse (377 KB of base64 against 147 KB).

PNG is not free either. It breaks the 8M-gas contract-creation policy unless it is shrunk, which changes the artwork anyway, and it costs about 54M more gas to store.

The only shown case where WebP does worse than PNG is Gallery.so's still preview, a minor venue where the artwork still renders. That does not outweigh direct evidence that the main marketplace shows this exact encoding.

The condition protects against the one thing no evidence covers: our exact roughly 1.2 MB tokenURI. Run that test before mainnet whichever format is chosen. Under the "unknown when inferred" rule, Blur, Etherscan, the closed-source wallets and iOS stay unknown. None has any evidence of rejecting WebP, and all of them render with WebP-capable decoders.
judge.condition:
Before mainnet, deploy the real 1/1 contract to Sepolia with the final tokenURI: the 'data:application/json;utf8,' JSON of about 1.2 MB, carrying the real still.webp and the real animation_url. This needs no private data, and nothing is sent to a third party except through the indexers' normal reading of the chain. Then check:
(a) Read tokenURI(1) back from the chain with a read-only eth_call through two public RPCs. Confirm it comes back complete, contains no '%' or '#', and that the image decodes to the PNG pixels.
(b) Alchemy getNFTMetadata through the eth-sepolia demo key. raw.error should be null, image.originalUrl should equal the on-chain data URI with every '+' intact, and image.cachedUrl or thumbnailUrl should show the still rather than a fallback. Check animation_url's '+' characters too.
(c) testnets.opensea.io: the item page should show the still and the HTML. Check that the i2c.seadn.io file name equals the MD5 of the WebP bytes.
(d) Optionally, MetaMask with the NFT added by hand on Sepolia.

If (c) fails, deploy a PNG variant on Sepolia before reverting. Only if the PNG passes where WebP fails is the problem the format; if both fail, the problem is size or encoding. In that case fix the tokenURI shape, not the image format.

Repo housekeeping when switching:
- contracts/docs/STORAGE.md line 130 still says "the still must be a PNG".
- contracts/scripts/stores.mjs line 29 still defaults to mint/still.png.
- The pack_page.py working copy already detects WebP from the file's bytes.
risks: The size is untested on every platform. No indexer or marketplace has been seen ingesting a data-URI tokenURI of about 1.1 to 1.3 MB; the largest observed was 325 KB (CryptoCoaster, on Alchemy). The largest observed WebP data-URI image is 10.5 KB, against our 110,572 bytes. This risk is the same for PNG (worse, at 377 KB of base64), and the Sepolia test covers it.

Alchemy is inconsistent with WebP data URIs. ShitPlunger (lossless WebP, 1536px) decoded to AVIF and PNG, but Tozzi Duck 200 and 201 still show the collection GIF even after refreshCache=true. Alchemy-backed apps could show a fallback or a tiny thumbnail; image.originalUrl keeps the data URI. Its cache has also shrunk non-PNG data rasters, for example a 256px BMP stored as a 120px AVIF.

Alchemy's '+'-to-space corruption. When a raw JSON tokenURI contains '%', Alchemy applies unquote_plus to every field, which breaks the base64 in both the image and the animation_url. pack_page.py refuses '%' and '#', so the 1/1 should be safe. That rests on two data points, and the ';utf8,' prefix combined with base64 '+' is untested. The risk is the same for either format.

Gallery.so: its reference backend (open-sourced 2026-04-13) has no case for data:image/webp, so the still would probably not show. The data:text/html animation is handled, so the token likely still displays. This is the only target where PNG is shown to work and WebP not, and production behaviour and site liveness are unverified.

Blur, Etherscan's NFT view, Coinbase Wallet / Base app, Zerion, Trust Wallet, Phantom, MetaMask Portfolio and Rainbow's backend were never observed with a data:image/webp token. Blur's image CDN decodes lossless WebP from a URL and its ingester stored a BMP data URI, but the full path is inferred. The others are closed or blocked behind bot checks.

Direct rendering in browsers or apps without WebP: iOS below 14, Safari on macOS 10.15 or older, IE11, Chrome 22 and older, Android 4.0 to 4.1. That is about 0.4% of global usage per caniuse. It matters only where an app puts the raw data URI in an ; OpenSea's CDN negotiates JPEG for such clients, and DeBank serves PNG.

Counter-example (weak): LikeCoin issue #27, in a 2025-05-12 comment, says an ipfs:// WebP showed 'content not available yet' on testnets.opensea.io. It involved IPFS on a testnet with an unknown WebP variant, and the mainnet observations above contradict it. Still, an OpenSea testnet failure in the Sepolia check should be cross-checked against a PNG variant before drawing conclusions.

Fidelity: OpenSea re-encodes to lossy WebP or JPEG thumbnails and DeBank to downscaled PNG, so viewers see a lossy copy, not the lossless pixels. Inferred: this is the same for PNG, so it is not a cost of WebP.

The repo docs and defaults still assume PNG (STORAGE.md line 130, stores.mjs line 29). If they are not updated, a deploy script could store still.png while the gas budget assumes WebP, or the reverse.

sweeps.summary:
Marketplace sweep, 2026-10-11. No marketplace documents WebP data URIs one way or the other. OpenSea's docs say "OpenSea supports most image formats, including SVG". Foundation, Zora and Manifold list no WebP for creator uploads, and Zora's coins SDK actively rejects image/webp.

The firm evidence comes from tests:
(1) A live Ethereum mainnet on-chain raster precedent. Brotchain 0xd31fc221d2b0e0321c43e9f6824b26ebfff01d7d returns a non-base64 'data:application/json,{...}' tokenURI whose image is 'data:image/bmp;base64,...' (confirmed with eth_call). OpenSea stores it as .bmp on i2c.seadn.io and serves it decoded as AVIF. Blur stores it as BMP (Cloudimage trace shows o<200:BMP>) and displays it as JPEG. So both decode generic data:image/* rasters and keep the format named in the data URI.
(2) Lossless VP8L decoding:
- OpenSea's CDN turned a VP8L original (raw2.seadn.io/currency_logos/TUSD.webp, served through i2c.seadn.io with ?format=png) into a PNG. It also turned a lossy VP8 NFT-platform asset into a PNG.
- Blur's images.blur.io (Scaleflex Cloudimage) turned Google's VP8L sample (gstatic 1_webp_ll.webp) into a 100x75 PNG.
- Rarible's media proxy (media.raribleuserdata.com/image/<base64 of source>) accepted a 'data:image/webp;base64' VP8L URI. It returned the exact 34 bytes as image/webp, so the viewer's browser does the decoding.

Net: OpenSea, Blur and Rarible are very likely to show a lossless WebP still correctly. Nobody has observed an actual data:image/webp NFT on these sites: a search for one on mainnet found none, and I did not deploy anything.

Two negatives:
- Gallery.so's open-source backend (gallery-so/gallery-backend, released 2026-04-13) has explicit cases for base64 PNG, JPEG, GIF, BMP and SVG data URIs but not WebP. 'data:image/webp;base64' falls to URITypeUnknown, and the raw URI string is then sniffed as text, so the still probably would not show there. The data:text/html animation is handled.
- Moralis says "currently WEBP and SVG are not supported" for its NFT previews. Moralis is outside this sweep but relevant.

Several targets are gone or do not apply:
- Foundation is offline. Its homepage reads "Foundation is offline", dated 27 April 2026, and help.foundation.app no longer resolves.
- Magic Eden closed its EVM marketplace in March 2026 (secondary reports; its evm-public API answered "no healthy upstream"). Its image CDN does decode VP8L.
- LooksRare collection pages return Error 500.
- Zora shows no external ERC-721s (/collect/eth:<Brotchain>/1 is PAGE NOT FOUND), and its coins SDK rejects webp.
- Manifold gallery: the contract does not use Manifold Creator Core, so it probably will not be listed there.

Side note for the orchestrator: OpenSea's metadata-storage doc lists only 'data:application/json;base64,' for tokenURI. Its contract-level example does use 'data:application/json;utf8,'. Brotchain's non-base64 'data:application/json,' tokenURI is indexed and displayed on OpenSea and Blur.

verdicts.evidence: DOCUMENTED: https://docs.opensea.io/docs/media-and-traits.md, image field: "OpenSea supports most image formats, including SVG, which OpenSea caches as PNG." The page says nothing about WebP. https://docs.opensea.io/docs/metadata-storage.md lists the Data URI form only as `data:application/json;base64,...`. https://docs.opensea.io/docs/contract-level-metadata.md shows `data:application/json;utf8,` for contractURI. Creator FAQ https://support.opensea.io/en/articles/8867028-creator-faq: "We currently support JPG, PNG, GIF, and SVG files for Drops". That is a Studio upload limit, not ingestion. OBSERVED: (a) eth_call tokenURI(1) on Brotchain 0xd31fc221d2b0e0321c43e9f6824b26ebfff01d7d (Ethereum mainnet, via publicnode) returns `data:application/json,{..."image":"data:image/bmp;base64,Qk02...` (89,102 chars). The opensea.io/collection/brotchain HTML lists imageUrl https://i2c.seadn.io/ethereum/0xd31fc.../3ca218db2a06079dc62e8988e5c4ea24.bmp, and that URL serves an AVIF image. So OpenSea decodes on-chain raster data URIs generically and keeps the format from the MIME. (b) https://i2c.seadn.io/currency_logos/TUSD.webp?format=png&w=50 returned a valid PNG. Its original on raw2.seadn.io is VP8L (lossless), so OpenSea's image service decodes lossless WebP. (c) A lossy VP8 original on i2c.seadn.io/stablechain/... with ?format=png also returned a PNG. INFERRED: a data:image/webp;base64 VP8L still will be ingested and shown. No data:image/webp NFT was found on OpenSea to confirm it end to end.

No Blur documentation on formats exists. OBSERVED: blur.io/eth/collection/brotchain, loaded in the browser pane, shows the BMP data-URI image (images.blur.io/_blur-prod/0xd31fc.../70038-230309fae98c6a97?w=128, naturalWidth 128). Response headers include x-cloudimg-traceid and x-hexa-flowtrace `AnR_F(webp_na)o<200:BMP>...`, so Blur stores the decoded data-URI bytes in their original format and Scaleflex Cloudimage transcodes them. Requesting https://images.blur.io/https://www.gstatic.com/webp/gallery3/1_webp_ll.webp?w=100 (a VP8L lossless sample) returned a 100x75 PNG with trace `o<200:WEBP>`, so Blur's CDN decodes lossless WebP. DOCUMENTED (Cloudimage): https://docs.cloudimage.io/transformations/input-formats lists WebP among supported origin formats (per search summary). INFERRED: a WebP data-URI still would be stored as WebP and shown.

DOCUMENTED (third-party only, weak): creator upload formats are "PNG, GIF, WEBP, MP4 and MP3" (bitpinas.com guide, size-charts.com). Rarible's API now requires a key (`Api Key is required`), so the item meta could not be read. OBSERVED: og.rarible.com serves images through https://media.raribleuserdata.com/image/<base64(source)>?width=... . Passing base64('data:image/webp;base64,UklGRhoAAABXRUJQVlA4TA0AAAAvAAAAEAcQERGIiP4HAA==') returned HTTP 200, content-type image/webp, exactly 34 bytes, a 1x1 VP8L. Passing the gstatic VP8L sample returned the original 81,836-byte VP8L untouched, even with format=png. So the proxy accepts WebP data URIs and passes WebP straight through; the viewer's browser decodes it, and all current browsers decode VP8L. The Brotchain item grid did not finish loading in the browser pane, so no on-chain example could be checked.

Secondary reports say Magic Eden closed its EVM and Bitcoin NFT markets around 9 March 2026: https://invezz.com/uk/news/2026/02/27/magic-eden-shuts-bitcoin-and-evm-nft-markets-to-refocus-on-solana/ . OBSERVED: api-mainnet.magiceden.dev/v4/evm-public/... answered `no healthy upstream`, and the v3 rtp ethereum endpoints answered `Not Found.`. The magiceden.io ETH collection page sat behind a Cloudflare bot check, which I did not bypass. The image CDN still works: https://img-cdn.magiceden.dev/rs:fill:200:200:0:0/plain/https://www.gstatic.com/webp/gallery3/1_webp_ll.webp@png returned a 200x200 PNG from a VP8L source. It refuses data: URIs as a source (`Source image is unreachable`). Probably no longer relevant for an ETH 1/1.

OBSERVED: the https://www.foundation.app/ homepage reads "Foundation is offline April 27, 2026 ... we have made the decision not to resume operations." help.foundation.app no longer resolves (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). Before it closed, its help articles (per search summaries) listed JPG, JPEG, PNG, SVG, GIF and, for imports, TIFF, WEBM and others, never WebP. Not applicable: the platform is closed.

OBSERVED: https://zora.co/collect/eth:0xd31fc221d2b0e0321c43e9f6824b26ebfff01d7d/1 renders "PAGE NOT FOUND". Zora now shows only its own coins/posts and no external ERC-721s, so it would not display this contract at all. DOCUMENTED IN CODE: ourzora/zora-protocol packages/coins-sdk/src/uploader/metadata.ts has validateImageMimeType allowing only png/jpeg/jpg/gif/svg+xml. Its test metadata.test.ts lists "image/webp" under invalid types: "Image must be a PNG, JPEG, JPG, GIF or SVG". The older legacy/protocol-sdk/src/ipfs/mimeTypes.ts isImage() does include "image/webp". Not applicable to an external 1/1.

Manifold's docs export (https://docs.manifold.xyz/llms-full.txt, 182 KB) has no 'webp', 'data:image' or file-type list. The old supported-file-types URL is a 404. The client SDK changelog says media.image is an "optimized preview (image_preview || thumbnail)", so Manifold makes its own previews with an undocumented pipeline. A GitHub search for "image/webp" in the manifoldxyz org found nothing. The 1/1 contract (contracts/src/KilimOneOfOne.sol) does not use Manifold Creator Core, so it probably would not appear in Manifold's gallery at all.

DOCUMENTED IN CODE: gallery-so/gallery-backend, "Initial open source release" dated 2026-04-13. In service/persist/token.go, TokenURI.Type() has explicit cases for data:image/svg+xml, bmp, png, jpeg and gif base64 URIs (URITypeBase64PNG etc.), and none for image/webp. 'data:image/webp;base64,...' falls to URITypeUnknown, and ToMediaType() returns MediaTypeUnknown. In service/media/media.go, PredictMediaType checks a file extension after the last '.'; base64 contains no '.', so it falls back to URI type and gets Unknown. In service/rpc/rpc.go, GetDataFromURIAsReader's default branch passes the raw URI string (`bytes.NewBuffer([]byte(turi))`) instead of decoding it, so sniffing sees text. For comparison, the PNG branch decodes and re-encodes, and webp only appears in the URL-extension map. The 'data:text/html' animation_url would be handled (URITypeBase64HTML). gallery.so still serves its site. INFERRED: the still would likely be missing or broken on Gallery while the HTML animation may render.

OBSERVED: https://looksrare.org/collections/0xd31fc221d2b0e0321c43e9f6824b26ebfff01d7d in the browser pane shows "Error 500 - Internal Server Error ... LooksBroken" with footer "© 2025 LooksRare". curl gets a Cloudflare 403. blockspot.io reports looksrare.org offline since 2026-07-27. I found no format documentation, and a GitHub code search of the LooksRare org for webp returned nothing. Effectively not working for NFT display.

corrections: Rarible: downgrade from 'likely' to 'unknown'. The proxy test only works for tiny URIs. I reran it: the 34-byte VP8L data URI does come back as HTTP 200 image/webp with the same 34 bytes. But a synthetic lossless WebP data URI of only about 5 KB (URL path about 5,020 chars) got HTTP 414 on two tries, as did ones of about 19 KB and about 53 KB. About 105 KB and about 213 KB (the real still's size class: 110,572 bytes means a URL of about 196 KB) failed with curl error 55. One early ~53 KB request returned 200 once and then 414 on retry. So media.raribleuserdata.com/image/<base64(data URI)> cannot carry the real still. How Rarible ingests and shows a real-size on-chain image (WebP or PNG) was not observed, and the creator-upload format list is third-party only.

OpenSea: the parts were re-checked and hold. raw2.seadn.io/currency_logos/TUSD.webp is RIFF/WEBP/VP8L (712 bytes), and i2c.seadn.io/...TUSD.webp?format=png&w=50 returns a 25x25 PNG. The Brotchain i2c.seadn.io .bmp URL serves image/avif (2,771 bytes). The end-to-end claim (a data:image/webp still in tokenURI gets ingested and shown) is still inferred. Relabel basis as 'inferred from observed components'. Under the default-to-unknown rule it would be 'unknown'. Treat it as a test-before-deploy item, not established. The precedent is also weak on size: Brotchain's whole tokenURI is about 89 KB, and ours is 1.1-1.3 MB. That gap is not specific to WebP, but the precedent shows nothing about ingesting a tokenURI that large.

Blur: re-checked and holds. images.blur.io/https://www.gstatic.com/webp/gallery3/1_webp_ll.webp?w=100 returns a 100x75 PNG with x-hexa-flowtrace 'An.R_F(webp_na)o<200:WEBP>...'. The CDN decodes VP8L when given a URL. The claim that Blur's ingester stores data-URI bytes and keeps the declared format rests on one BMP example, so the end-to-end verdict is inferred too. Same relabel as OpenSea: 'likely' only as an inference, 'unknown' under the strict rule.

Gallery.so: the code reading holds. I re-fetched service/persist/token.go from gallery-so/gallery-backend (repo created and last pushed 2026-04-13). TokenURI.Type() has base64 cases for svg+xml, bmp, png, jpeg, gif, wav and mpeg and none for webp, so 'data:image/webp;base64,...' falls to URITypeUnknown. rpc.go line 389's default branch does bytes.NewBuffer([]byte(turi)). media.go maps 'webp' only as a URL extension. Three caveats the sweep missed. (a) The README calls the repo 'published as reference', so it may not match production, and whether gallery.so is still indexing was not verified: its homepage is a JS shell whose only text is 'Gallery'. (b) In tokenprocessing/pipeline.go, if the image fails but the base64 data:text/html animation succeeds and requireImg is false, the token still gets media from the animation. So the token would probably still display through the HTML, with only the still missing. (c) The basis should be 'documented in code (reference release), production unverified', not 'documented'.

The sweep never set the PNG baseline against WebP. Gallery.so would handle data:image/png (URITypeBase64PNG), so Gallery is the one target where WebP is shown to do worse than the current PNG. The Rarible proxy limit and the 1.1-1.3 MB tokenURI ingest question hit PNG equally (the PNG is worse: about 377 KB base64).

Foundation (offline), Zora (no external ERC-721 pages), Magic Eden EVM (closed) and LooksRare (Error 500) are fine as 'not applicable' or 'unknown'. I did not re-fetch them because they do not change the decision.

A further search found no documented or observed mainnet NFT whose image is data:image/webp;base64, and no report contradicting OpenSea or Blur WebP support. Absence of a precedent remains the main gap.

sweeps.summary:
Sweep of indexers and NFT APIs, done 2026-10-11. Scratch files are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-orkhan-Documents-ChatGPT-kilim/312fc50c-c278-46b4-8c02-9f5c98c46bda/scratchpad/idx-sweep/. Nothing in the repo was changed. I could not find any live mainnet token whose image is a data:image/webp URI, so none of the targets was observed rendering this exact format. The verdicts below rest on four things: how each pipeline handles other data: rasters (PNG and BMP, observed), what the image CDNs say they accept (WebP input is documented), and source code where it exists. The repo's still.webp header was confirmed as RIFF/WEBP/VP8L.

Main results:
(1) Alchemy's 30,000-byte limit. The exact text, in the "Contract returned a broken token URI" section of https://www.alchemy.com/docs/reference/nft-api-faq, is "This can also happen if the content length of the response is larger than 30 000 bytes." It sits under a heading about a tokenUri that "does not respond to the web request", so it covers HTTP fetches. It did not apply to data: URIs in practice: Alchemy fully parsed on-chain data: tokenURIs of 59,349 bytes (Terraforms), 89,102 bytes (Brotchain) and 325,521 bytes (CryptoCoaster). A tokenURI of 1.1 to 1.3 MB is untested.
(2) Alchemy stored an on-chain data:image/png byte for byte. On Polygon, the contract 0xB4D3973637369692981C7C40f7a733a04b2D0E9c (token 2) gave cachedUrl content-type image/png at 2,834 bytes, identical to the on-chain bytes. Thumbnails there come from Cloudflare Images (nft2-cdn.alchemy.com/cdn-cgi/image/...), and older entries use Cloudinary. Cloudflare's docs list WebP as an input format.
(3) A raw-JSON tokenURI can have its "+" characters turned into spaces by Alchemy, and this is not specific to WebP. CryptoCoaster's raw tokenURI ('data:application/json,{...}') contains 376 '%' characters. In Alchemy's raw.metadata.image and image.originalUrl, every '+' became a space ('data:image/svg xml;base64,...' with 16 spaces), so the base64 no longer decodes. Its cachedUrl was still correct. Brotchain's raw tokenURI has no '%', and all 10,132 '+' characters came through intact. The 1/1's packer already refuses '%' and '#' (onchain/pack_page.py data_url_text), so the output should be pure JSON plus base64 and fall on the safe side. The 1/1's ';utf8,' form is untested on Alchemy.
(4) OpenSea's pipeline decodes on-chain data: raster images whatever their MIME type. Brotchain's data:image/bmp is stored as ...75fda75a0b3f7f33eeaffa71ddedfe36.bmp on i2c.seadn.io and served as AVIF or JPEG. OpenSea's media docs say "most image formats" and never name WebP or data URIs.
(5) Reservoir and SimpleHash are both shut down. Reservoir: sunset announced for 2025-10-15, and api.reservoir.tools now returns NXDOMAIN. SimpleHash: Alchemy's migration blog says it sunset on 2025-03-27, and its API now returns a 301 that points back to itself. Coinbase Wallet therefore no longer goes through SimpleHash, and I found no public source naming its current provider.
(6) Moralis lists WEBP among supported preview formats. QuickNode documents no media processing at all. Etherscan's NFT page could not be checked: it sits behind a Cloudflare bot check, which I did not try to get past.

Lossless versus lossy: every pipeline above decodes or transcodes through standard image stacks (Cloudflare Images, Cloudinary, OpenSea's CDN), and libwebp has decoded VP8L since 2012. I found no evidence that any of these treats lossless WebP differently from lossy, but that part is inferred, not observed. One real gap is untested: a tokenURI of about 1.2 MB with a data:image/webp of about 147 KB of base64 on any of these indexers. A Sepolia test deploy queried through Alchemy's public 'demo' key (eth-sepolia) would settle the Alchemy and OpenSea part without any mainnet risk.

sweeps.summary: Wallets sweep, 2026-10-11. In every open-source wallet I checked, nothing filters out WebP or a data: image. That covers MetaMask extension, MetaMask mobile, the MetaMask core NftController, Rainbow, Rabby and Ledger Live. I found no MIME allow-list and no svg/png-only filter. The only data: checks I found are a phishing check in MetaMask core that looks only at http(s) URLs, Rabby's http(s)-only rule for video/audio, and Rainbow skipping CDN signing for data: URIs. **Where wallets get the image.** Most of them do not decode the on-chain data URI themselves. They show a copy hosted by an indexer: - MetaMask's NFT API (nft.api.cx.metamask.io) now returns OpenSea CDN URLs. It was Reservoir-shaped before. - Rabby uses DeBank (api.rabby.io / static.debank.com). - Rainbow uses its own key-gated GraphQL backend (arc), which keeps SimpleHash's field names, and resizes through imgix or its own image CDN. - Ledger Live removed its NFT gallery in September 2025 (PRs #11746, #11787, #11841). It now sends users to OpenSea or Magic Eden. **Reference token (observed).** Tozzi Duck Machine, 0x0cd9c257f7565476f5d374ef27854abdd5916bad, token 200, is a live mainnet ERC-721. Its tokenURI image is data:image/webp;base64 and the file is lossless (VP8L, 760 bytes). It is far smaller than the Kilim still; the format matches, the size does not. - The MetaMask NFT API returns an i2c.seadn.io/…/.webp URL for tokens 200–203. - That OpenSea CDN serves lossy WebP (VP8) when the Accept header is */* or includes image/webp. It serves JPEG when Accept is only png/jpeg, with or without ?width=250 or ?width=1000. - Rabby's API returns DeBank-hosted PNGs for tokens 201 and 202: a 512×512 'content' image and a 256×256 thumbnail. So the two indexers I could observe both read a lossless WebP data URI and re-encode it into formats every client handles. Users will mostly see a lossy or resized copy, not the exact lossless pixels. **Where wallets render the data: URI directly:** - MetaMask extension: plain . The extension's MV3 content security policy has no img-src or default-src limit. - MetaMask mobile: expo-image 57.0.5, which uses Glide's data: loader on Android and SDWebImage with libwebp 1.6.0 on iOS. - Rainbow: a data: URI is not sent to the CDN and goes to the plain React Native Image. URLs ending in .webp go to react-native-fast-image, which has the WebP coder and libwebp 1.5.0. - Rabby: an antd . All of these decode lossless WebP. Chromium and Firefox handle it. Android decodes lossless WebP from 4.2.1. iOS needs version 14 or later (Safari 14: "Added WebP image support."). I also ran macOS 26.6.2's built-in image decoder (ImageIO, via sips) on still.webp: the output is pixel-identical to still.png (same SHA-256 of the RGB pixels). iOS uses the same decoder framework family, but I did not run an iOS device or simulator. **Remaining risks:** - Devices older than iOS 14 / macOS 11 with an app that has no bundled libwebp. Safari 14 on macOS Catalina is the inferred case. - Coinbase Wallet / Base app, Zerion, Trust Wallet and Phantom are closed source and their indexers need API keys, so those verdicts are inferred, not observed. - The 1.1–1.3 MB tokenURI may stress indexers. The Tozzi token is tiny, so it says nothing about size. - MetaMask's on-chain fallback for manually added NFTs calls fetch() on the raw 'data:application/json;utf8,' string. Any '#' in the JSON text would cut the string off there; '%' may be URL-decoded and break the JSON. This does not affect the format choice, but someone should check the final JSON for these characters. Scratch files (Tozzi tokenURI, decoded WebP, pixel-compare script, sparse clones) are in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-orkhan-Documents-ChatGPT-kilim/312fc50c-c278-46b4-8c02-9f5c98c46bda/scratchpad/wallets-webp/.

Re-decoding that PNG gave RGB SHA-256 6dc07a35…259dc, identical to still.png. That shows Apple ImageIO decodes this exact VP8L file losslessly; iOS 14+ uses the same framework family, but I did not run an iOS device or simulator.

corrections: Ledger Live verdict 'yes / observed' is a category error. Ledger Live no longer renders NFT images: only NftEntryPoint remains in apps/ledger-live-desktop and apps/ledger-live-mobile, and no gallery or media components are left in the 46bd13a tree. Change it to 'not applicable (no in-app NFT rendering)'. What a Ledger user sees depends on the OpenSea or Magic Eden webview, and those belong in the marketplace sweep.

MetaMask extension/mobile, the 'manually added NFTs show the raw data:image/webp' claim: MetaMask/core NftController.ts (around lines 797-812) merges `image: nftApiMetadata?.image ?? blockchainMetadata?.image`. On mainnet with Display NFT media on, the NFT API (OpenSea CDN) image wins even for manually added NFTs. The raw data URI is used only when the API has no image, for example if OpenSea failed to index the 1.1-1.3 MB JSON. With the toggle off, the on-chain path returns image:null, so a placeholder shows instead (#getNftInformationFromTokenURI, around lines 663-672).

The 'Direct data: rendering' parts of the MetaMask extension, MetaMask mobile, Rainbow and Rabby verdicts are source-read inference, not observed. No wallet build was run and no data URI was rendered in one. Only the indexer path (MetaMask NFT API to i2c.seadn.io, and the Rabby API to static.debank.com) was observed. I re-ran both and they reproduce exactly.

The reference-token caveat understates the differences. Tozzi Duck 200's tokenURI is 'data:application/json;base64,...' (re-fetched via eth_call on publicnode), not the raw 'data:application/json;utf8,{...}' the Kilim uses, and its WebP is 760 bytes, not 110 KB inside a ~1.2 MB string. The observed indexer results show only that the WebP-in-data-URI format is ingested. They do not show that a utf8 JSON data URI of this size gets through OpenSea, DeBank or the MetaMask fallback.

'Users will mostly see a lossy or resized copy' is not caused by the format choice. OpenSea and DeBank re-encode whatever they ingest, and would very likely do the same to the PNG (inferred; an on-chain PNG token's CDN output was not tested). Do not present it as a cost of WebP.

Following the 'default to unknown when inferred' rule, these should go from 'likely' to 'unknown': MetaMask Portfolio (indexer not verified), Rainbow (arc backend key-gated, upstream unknown), Rabby mobile (same API, but the app was not checked), Coinbase Wallet/Base, Zerion and Phantom. Rabby mobile is the strongest of these, because its API was observed returning PNG copies of on-chain VP8L tokens.

MetaMask extension CSP: I confirmed that app/manifest/v3/chrome.json extension_pages has no img-src or default-src (fetched from GitHub main). The Firefox manifest was not checked (fetch returned nothing), so 'Firefox ' for the extension is inferred.

Missed risk, unverified: if MetaMask or any client takes the on-chain fallback, it needs a public or provider RPC to return a ~1.2 MB eth_call result. Provider response-size or gas caps were not tested. This does not depend on PNG vs WebP, and the smaller WebP slightly reduces it.

sweeps.summary:
On-chain precedent sweep for 'data:image/webp;base64' in tokenURI "image".

I found and checked three live contracts with read-only eth_call. The script is call.py in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-orkhan-Documents-ChatGPT-kilim/312fc50c-c278-46b4-8c02-9f5c98c46bda/scratchpad/webp-precedent/ and the decoded images are in out/.

1. The Amazing Tozzi Duck Machine. ERC-721 on Ethereum mainnet, 0x0cd9c257f7565476f5d374ef27854abdd5916bad. tokenURI(200) and tokenURI(201) return base64 JSON with "image":"data:image/webp;base64,...". The bytes are RIFF/WEBP with a VP8L chunk, so the image is LOSSLESS, 400x400, 760 B and 362 B. Token 200 has the attribute Creator = Matt Furie. Token ids 0-199 revert.
2. ShitPlunger. ERC-1155 on Ethereum mainnet, 0x01cecf7a8F0095fa622Ff03D714fD2244548Da35. uri(1) returns a LOSSLESS (VP8L) image at 1536x1536, 10,482 B. This is the closest to our case (1536x2048 VP8L), but about 10 times smaller in bytes.
3. Geoplets. ERC-721 on Base, 0x999ac3b6571fefb770ea3a836e82cc45cd1e653f. tokenURI(20086) and tokenURI(22420) return LOSSY (VP8) WebP at 512x512. A second Geoplets address listed in the repo README, 0x9e10..40E0, reverts.

Art Blocks' public abx toolkit (github.com/ArtBlocks/abx) also writes on-chain images with a declared type for PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and AVIF, and has a test asserting '"image":"data:image/webp;base64,'. That shows tooling support, not a test of how marketplaces display it.

How it displays:

**OpenSea (observed, positive).** The public item pages for Tozzi Duck 200 and 201, ShitPlunger 1 and Geoplet 20086 all carry an "imageUrl" on i2c.seadn.io. In every case the CDN filename is exactly the MD5 of the decoded on-chain WebP bytes:
- Duck 200: fc1d1e92..., matches.
- Duck 201: 3a2e4064..., matches.
- Plunger: fedc189b..., matches.
- Geoplet: 88c32fbf..., matches.

So OpenSea fetched, decoded and processed the data-URI WebP. The CDN serves content-type image/webp, but re-encoded as LOSSY VP8 thumbnails: duck 400 px, about 9 KB; plunger downscaled from 1536 to 500 px. Viewed side by side, the duck 200 thumbnail matches the on-chain pixels.

**Rarible (observed, positive).** The og:image is media.raribleuserdata.com proxying api.rarible.org/content/embedded/<sha256>. The sha256 equals the on-chain WebP bytes. It serves image/webp byte-for-byte, still VP8L. The Rarible page for the ERC-1155 plunger returns 404, and the duck 201 page title is stale.

**Alchemy NFT API, demo key, no refresh (observed, mixed).** ShitPlunger 1 (last updated 2025-12-07) decoded correctly: cached AVIF and a 500 px PNG that shows the plunger. Duck 200 and 201 (last updated May 2025) instead show a 2,059,620 B GIF. Its MD5, 42cfac34..., is the OpenSea collection image of Tozzi Ducks, so Alchemy fell back to the collection image for those tokens. I infer that Alchemy may have added data-URI WebP support between those dates, or failed on those tokens for another reason. originalUrl correctly holds the WebP data URI in both cases.

**Etherscan, Magic Eden, Blockscout (not determined).** All three return a Cloudflare 403 or challenge to curl. A WebFetch of Etherscan's NFT page shows a placeholder (empty-token.png) and an image from static.looksnice.org. That proxy returns S3 AccessDenied for these tokens and also for a BAYC control, so nothing can be concluded from it.

**Counter-example (documented, weak).** In LikeCoin issue #27 (2025-01-31), the team states "webp does not work in image field" on testnets.opensea.io (Sepolia, IPFS-hosted webp; 'content not available yet'). They planned to convert webp to gif and later closed it as "Rare case." I could not fetch the file to check whether it was animated or extended WebP, because the IPFS gateways returned 429/404. It also involved IPFS and testnets rather than an on-chain data URI, and our mainnet observations contradict it. I found no project documented as switching an on-chain data-URI image from WebP to PNG.

**Caveats.** Every verified precedent is a small image, 10.5 KB at most, against our 110,572 B. None is a 1/1 with an HTML animation_url. Display in wallets (MetaMask, Rainbow and others) and on Zora, Foundation and Manifold was not covered by this sweep.

verdicts.target: Browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari incl. iOS) rendering the precedent images
verdicts.evidence: Not tested in a browser in this sweep. OpenSea and Rarible serve these tokens to browsers as image/webp (OpenSea re-encodes to VP8; Rarible serves the original VP8L), which implies normal browser WebP support. macOS sips decoded all on-chain VP8L and VP8 files correctly in my scratch dir.

corrections: OpenSea, confirmed by rerun (observed). A fresh eth_call via ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com gave the same bytes for Tozzi Duck 200 and 201 and ShitPlunger 1: RIFF/WEBPVP8L, 760 / 362 / 10,482 B, MD5 fc1d1e92... / 3a2e4064... / fedc189b.... Pixel comparison against the on-chain image (PIL): mean absolute difference per channel is about 0.7/255 for the plunger at 1000px and about 2-3/255 for the duck. So OpenSea decoded the LOSSLESS data-URI WebP. Limit: the largest image tested is 10.5 KB and 1536px, against our 110,572 B and 1536x2048. Note that OpenSea serves a lossy re-encode whatever the input format. That the same happens to PNG input is inferred, not tested; if so, lossless fidelity on OpenSea is the same for PNG and WebP.

OpenSea has no documentation naming WebP. Its media docs say only that it supports 'most image formats' (docs.opensea.io/docs/media-and-traits). The OpenSea 'yes' rests on observation only and should be labelled that way.

Rarible, confirmed (observed). https://api.rarible.org/content/embedded/624c14d7c9f4999d266d51bdd6748b111a2965305eb1e55203b3d83abeef91c1 returns 200 image/webp, byte-identical to the on-chain VP8L of duck 200. The duck contract source shows the image is always data:image/webp from SSTORE2 and never changes, so the ducks are real failures, not stale data from an earlier image. The current image backends for Coinbase Wallet, MetaMask and Magic Eden are unknown and need separate checks.
